New components, because a file manager kept building them itself: `TextField` and `TextArea`, `FieldRow` and `FieldRowGroup`, `PathField`, `GlyphField`, `Tree`, `Table`, `RowMark`, `GlyphTile`, `ListRow` and `IconButton`, all in React and Vue. `Button`, `Toggle`, `Selector`, `Window`, `Select`, `ContextMenu`, `SidebarRow`, `Card`, `SubCard`, `PasswordField`, `CopyField` and the toasts take the hooks an app kept working around, and a few small bugs are gone.

**Adopting apps:**

- **Moving up:** install `@glimstone/core` with `@glimstone/react` or `@glimstone/vue` at 4.1.1, all at the same number. Nothing is renamed or removed.
- **Fields:** a raw `<input class="glim-input">` can become a `TextField`, and a width class of the app's own can become `width="short"`, `"medium"`, `"wide"` or `"grow"`. A rule of the app's own for `textarea.glim-input` can go.
- **Rows:** a row of the app's own can become a `FieldRow`. The controls inside it drop their `label`, and `Toggle` also drops `hideLabel`, since the row draws the words.
- **A field's focus:** `.glim-input` and `.glim-num-field` no longer show the focus ring (rule 14). If an app restyled a field's focus around the ring, look at it again.
- **Buttons in a flex row:** a `Button` no longer shrinks to an ellipsis. Whatever stands beside it gives way. An app's own `flex` rule for a button still wins, and its own `flex: none` can go.
- **Window feet:** buttons in `.glim-modal-foot` hug their words down to the smallest width floor, 5.5rem, so the row is tighter than it was. The start text wraps before a button drops to the next line, and a foot without room wraps its buttons. An app's own `flex` on `.glim-window-start` can go. A pair that has to match still passes `stage`.
- **Toasts:** a toast is 24rem wide, an action stands under the message, and a path breaks after a slash. On a phone a toast takes the window's width and the newest two show. An app's own rules for the action can go.
- **Key buttons and gaps:** `class="glim-btn-key"` can become `size="key"`, and `<span class="glim-icon-btn-gap">` beside a `v-if` can become `absent`. The classes stay.
- **Toggle in light mode:** the off track is darker, `#8d8d8d`, and holds 3:1 against a card and against its knob. An app that set its own off colour can drop it.
- **Inside a well or a sub-card:** a `Select` trigger and a `Pill` step up one surface, as a field does. A `NumberField` does so in a well too.
- **Toggle in Vue:** an `id`, a data attribute or a listener passed to `Toggle` lands on the switch, not on its frame. `class` and `style` stay on the frame, so a script that went looking for the switch inside the frame can drop that.
- **Selector in Vue:** `update:modelValue` hands a plain id with one choice and a list with `select="many"`, so a cast around the handler can go.
- **Flutter:** move the git dependency to `ref: v4.1.1`. `GlimTheme` gains `toggleOff`. Nothing else changes there.
- **Version:** `GLIMSTONE_VERSION` from `@glimstone/core` reads 4.1.1.

## ✨ Added

- **`TextField` and `TextArea`**: a line of text and a few lines of text, borderless and filled, in the widths `short`, `medium`, `wide` and `grow`, with `mono` for a path or a token. `PasswordField`, `CopyField` and `PathField` take the same `width`.
- **`FieldRow`**: the name at the start of a row with an "(i)", its controls together at the end. `Toggle`, `Selector`, `Select`, `TextField`, `TextArea`, `PasswordField`, `NumberField`, `CopyField`, `PathField`, `Slider` and `Combobox` take their accessible name from the row, and `useFieldName` gives an app's own control the same. A click on the name focuses a field or flips a switch. A row with only a value shows it as a pill.
- **`FieldRowGroup`**: rows in it share one column for their names, as wide as the longest, so fields that grow start at one edge. With `columns={2}` the rows stand in two columns that each line up their own names, and a `wide` row spans both.
- **`PathField`**: a path and a button that asks the app for one through a `pick` callback, so GlimStone does not need to know where the folders come from. With less than 20rem of room, or with `compact`, the button shows its glyph alone.
- **`Tree`**: a hierarchy loaded as it opens, with the keys of the WAI-ARIA tree. A folder picker opens one, and it fits any other hierarchy too.
- **`GlyphField`**: a field with a glyph inside it, such as a filter or a search, and `after` for controls inside the box.
- **`Table`**: a short list of facts in columns, from `columns` and `rows`, with a cell of the caller's own and a quiet `more` line.
- **`GlyphTile`**: a small holder for a glyph. It fills with the accent while the row around it is reached.
- **`RowMark`**: the round mark on a row picked for an action on many (rule 39).
- **`ListRow`**: a tile, a name with an "(i)", badges and buttons that come in on hover and focus (rule 6). With a click handler the whole row opens its object, by keyboard too.
- **`IconButton`**: a glyph in a square in every label mode, for a row that keeps its text. `href` makes it a link, `pressed` a button that stays on or off, and `absent` holds the place of a button a row does not have. Everything else with one action stays a `Button` with `variant="icon"`.
- **`Button`** takes `href`, which makes it a link with the button's look, and `before` and `after` (slots in Vue) for a count or a key cap inside it. `size="key"` gives the second height. `compact` and `compactBelow` leave the glyph alone where the words have no room, and a compact button with a count grows to hold it. In React, `Button` and `IconTipButton` pass the other props of a `<button>` on, as they already do in Vue.
- **`Select` with `rows="menu"`**: the open list draws the rows of a `ContextMenu`, so an app that has both shows one kind of menu row. The keys, the wheel and the typing stay the select's. `triggerAttrs` go on the trigger, and `listId` is the open list's id.
- **Menu ids:** `ContextMenu` takes an `id`, a menu item a `subId` for the submenu it opens, and a menu of `MenuBar` an `id` of its own.
- **`SidebarRow`** can go without `href`, which makes it a button. `before` and `after` (slots in Vue) hold a tree's toggle, a meter or a pin, and a click anywhere else still goes to the row. A row with slots is never centred, so they stay in reach in every label mode. `depth` steps a tree's row in by its level, with a smaller glyph and gap, so a deep name keeps its room.
- **`Selector`** takes numeric ids, `attrs` on an item for its segment, and `onPress` (`@press` in Vue), which hears every press, also one on the segment already chosen.
- **`Window`** takes `attrs` on an action for its button, and hands over its card element: `ref` in React, the exposed `card` in Vue.
- **Markup in a notch:** `drawn` in React and the `title` slot in Vue hold a count or an unsaved dot on a `Card` or a `Window`. A window's `title` alone stays its name.
- **A toast's action:** an entry takes `action`, a button such as Undo, under the message. A press runs it and dismisses the toast.
- **`SubCard`** can go without a title.
- **`PasswordField`** exposes its `input` in Vue and takes `eyeAttrs` for the eye.

## 🎨 Design

- **Rule 13: `IconButton` is the one button that stays a glyph in every label mode.** It goes in list rows and dense toolbars only, and rule 38 names it as the ghost that never prints a word.
- **Rule 26: a tree is not a fold.** A fold hides a part of a page, and a tree's rows are the content being walked through.
- **Rule 35: `FieldRow` is the row.** It names the control, and a click on the name reaches it. A `<label>` around the row would do that too, but it breaks a selector's strip.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **`Toggle`** put its attributes on the frame in Vue and took none in React, while an id or a data hook belongs on the switch.
- **`.glim-input` and `.glim-num-field`** showed the global focus ring against rule 14. Focus shows as the fill stepping up the ramp.
- **`Button` in a flex row** shrank to an ellipsis once its words passed the width floor. In a window's foot, beside a long start text, this was easy to hit.
- **`Selector` with `pairsOnPhone`** cut its labels below 600px, and with three rows of segments its pill track went lumpy. The labels wrap and the track takes a card's corners.
- **`Toggle` off in the light theme** was hard to see against a card.
- **`Card` in Vue** added a space after the title.
- **`.glim-input` in a `SubCard`** vanished into its ground, since it only stepped up in a `.glim-well`.
- **A closed `Select`** left an empty box on the body. The box stays, since the machine needs it, but it takes no room.
